items_missed: 1_set_agenda: No greeting, no 'how are you,' no move-date availability check, no agenda statement, and no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation — the call went straight into troubleshooting the customer's photo-sharing issue.

2_probe: No origin address/zip captured, no special considerations (hallways, tight turns), no storage-unit question, no additional-stops question, no access/HOA/parking question, and no moving-stressor question.

3_pricing: No 'pricing is super simple' opener, no packing-service pricing explained (despite asking if she wanted packing service), no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee.
4_clock: Didn't say the clock starts when the contract opens on-site, and never did a sense-check ('does that make sense?') after walking through pricing.
5_estimate: No walk-distance callout and no equivalent/analogy (e.g., school bus reference) to help the customer picture crew size or truck load.
6_save_your_ass: Entire prep speech skipped — no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no 'prep now = shorter move = lower bill' framing.
7_quote_booking: No attempt to book/lock the move in today, no explicit no-deposit-required mention, no 'reply with any corrections' instruction, and no hours/contact info given before hanging up.
8_politeness: Used the customer's first name only once ('Anna') — relied on 'ma'am' almost exclusively instead.

9_bonus: No insurance explanation (No Worries coverage / 60 cents-per-lb baseline), and didn't proactively address likely FAQs or offer budget-conscious framing after the customer said she was 'shopping around.'
top_strength: Jeline stayed patient and steady through nearly ten minutes of the customer struggling to share photos, then recovered the call smoothly with 'That's okay ma'am, if you cannot send it, that's okay — do you think you could just tell me what are the items from the garage?' The item-by-item inventory that followed (mobility scooter, wheelchairs, TVs by size, dining set, washer/dryer) was thorough and specific.
coaching_note: Your inventory-gathering once you pivoted off the photo problem was genuinely excellent — detailed and patient. But none of the core sales fundamentals showed up: no agenda statement, no Save Your Ass prep speech, no damage coverage or Meet Your Mover pitch, and no attempt to book the move or offer the no-deposit close. When the customer said 'I'm shopping around,' that was exactly the moment to differentiate with the guarantees and try to lock her in — instead the call just ended with 'I'll get back to you.' Build yourself a simple mental checklist for pricing and booking so those pieces come out even when a call gets derailed early by something unrelated.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and even-keeled through a frustrating tech detour and earned a genuine 'that was fun' from the customer, but otherwise stayed transactional with few affirmations or empathy statements and near-exclusive use of 'ma'am' instead of the customer's name.
